On repository-scoped knowledge.

Knowledge that belongs to one repository travels with that repository. Knowledge
that belongs to the organisation is referenced, not copied, so that a change of
organisational direction does not require editing every repository that depends
on it.

A reference records a stable identifier, a semantic digest, the authority that
published it, and the interval over which it was observed valid. It does not
record the prose. Resolving a reference requires an authorized live capability
against the publishing authority.

The consequence of losing a reference differs by repository. A repository whose
safety argument depends on the referenced rule loses more than one that merely
cites it for context, so each repository records its own dependence class and the
stricter of the two classes governs.
